summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with HLA-B27-positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and obesity, was admitted for severe right sacroiliac joint and hip pain rated 10/10, limiting mobility and causing urinary accidents. He had self-initiated a prednisone taper and increased hydromorphone use at home without adequate relief. Labs showed elevated CRP indicating inflammation, but no infection. He was managed with IV pain control initially, transitioned to PCA, then to oral OxyContin and oxycodone. Rheumatology supported the steroid taper, and orthopedics ruled out hip effusion. Pain and mobility improved significantly by discharge. He was discharged home on a short prednisone taper, long-acting and breakthrough opioids, with follow-up planned in rheumatology and pain clinics. Concerns remain about untreated ankylosing spondylitis due to prior discontinuation of biologics over infection fears.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of multiple sites in spine
Long term (current) use of systemic steroids
